title: CPF property use and the 95-year lease requirement
asked: Mr Foo Cexiang asked whether the CPF Board will align the life expectancy factor with the Department of Statistics Singapore's 83.5-year average when calculating how much CPF savings can be used to buy a property, instead of the current 95 years.
response: Mr Chee Hong Tat said CPF property rules aim to encourage Singaporeans to buy a home for life, protecting housing and retirement adequacy. Under the Home for Life condition, the remaining lease must cover the youngest owner until at least age 95; if the requirement were 83.5 years, many seniors would live longer than that average. He said MND and HDB will look at appropriate ways to help the two groups Mr Foo described, while keeping the 95-year safeguard, and that they are open to reviewing other possibilities.

key_points.point: CPF property rules are meant to encourage buying a home for life, which safeguards housing and retirement adequacy.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: our rules on Central Provident Fund (CPF) usage for property purchases are intended to encourage Singaporeans to buy a home for life, which safeguards their housing and retirement adequacy.

key_points.point: Under the Home for Life condition, the remaining lease must cover the youngest owner until at least age 95.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: Under the current Home for Life condition, the remaining lease must cover the youngest owner till at least age 95.

key_points.point: Setting the requirement at 83.5 years would mean many seniors live longer than that average lifespan.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: if we set the requirement at 83.5 years, many seniors would live longer than this average lifespan.

key_points.point: Mr Foo described residents renting on the open market whose incomes are too high for HDB rental but who cannot own private property.
key_points.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
key_points.quote: Their incomes are too high to rent Housing and Development Board (HDB) flats, but at the same time they cannot own in the private sector.

key_points.point: He also described long-term HDB renters who are a couple of years short of an affordable lease because of the 95-year requirement.
key_points.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
key_points.quote: because of this 95-year-old requirement, they are a couple of years short of a lease tenure of a price that they will be able to afford to own their own HDB flat.

key_points.point: MND and HDB will look at appropriate ways to help these individuals.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: the Ministry of National Development and HDB will take a look and see what are some of the appropriate ways that we can help these individuals.

key_points.point: The Minister said help should be for a home that lasts for life, making the 95-year safeguard important.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: this safeguard of ensuring that the remaining lease can last them till at least age 95 is an important one.

key_points.point: He said they are open to reviewing other ways to help.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: If there are other ways in which we can help them, I think we are open to reviewing and looking at different possibilities.

left_open: Whether the CPF Board will align the life expectancy factor with the Department of Statistics Singapore's 83.5-year average.
What specific measures, if any, will be introduced for the two groups of residents Mr Foo described.
supplementary: Residents unable to start home ownership because of the 95-year lease requirement, and a request for HDB to review their cases.
